title: Substrate unreliability is the reason, not an obstacle, for biological intelligence

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Substrate unreliability is the reason, not an obstacle, for biological intelligence

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Levin argues that the noise and unreliability of biological matter is a feature rather than a bug: morphological and behavioural intelligence arose because of, not in spite of, the vulnerability of the substrate, as suggested by planaria having the noisiest genome and the best regeneration and cancer resistance.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 6. What It Means, and What Next: A Research Program for Further Development

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It seems that the underlying noise and unreliability of biological matter is not a bug but a feature: we obtained morphological (and behavioral) intelligence because of, not in spite of, the vulnerability of the substrate45.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “6. What It Means, and What Next: A Research Program for Further Development”. Scope: Living organisms, especially metazoans

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-12: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.41

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public comparative data can test limited correlations, but the causal claim that vulnerability produced intelligence is a historical inference with strong confounding and very broad scope. Existing data cannot decisively separate it from common-cause or reverse explanations.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across species, estimate substrate instability, regenerative and behavioural flexibility, then test whether instability predicts those competencies after phylogenetic and life-history controls. A robust positive relation supports the proposed association, but causal origin would require stronger evolutionary evidence.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Planarian genome noisiness may not generalize.

Substrate unreliability and intelligence lack agreed cross-species measures.

Comparative association cannot identify why intelligence evolved.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.3
analysis feasibility: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.45
data existence: 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Genome repositories make the noise side of the comparison measurable, and regeneration can be compiled from the literature for a coarse test of co-occurrence. That is only a proxy for a historical causal claim. Many life-history and phylogenetic confounds remain, and no existing dataset records the evolutionary counterfactual the claim requires.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across metazoan genomes, rank repeat content, heterozygosity, and assembly difficulty against independent scores of regenerative completeness and cancer incidence. A positive relationship would fit the suggestion; a negative or null relationship would count against it. The historical because-of claim still needs a design that separates cause from correlate.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Planaria are one clade, so they cannot establish a general evolutionary cause.

Regeneration and cancer incidence are not coded in the genome databases.

A cross-species correlation cannot show that intelligence arose because of substrate noise.
